title: Phase-interleave pin lab (personal)
content:
Purpose
- Quick lab notebook for an idea: interleaving pinned version cohorts across overlapping phases instead of a single monotonic warmup. Goal: reduce noisy cold-starts, smooth tail latency, and enable rolling pin/unpin with minimal traffic oscillation.

Notes / motivation
- We see spikes when large cohorts unpin/pin around the same window (batch warmups + cache warm). If we stagger by sub-cohorts and alternate pin states, we can keep a baseline of primed caches while allowing incremental rollback.
- This is primarily targeted for Dedicated and Private customers with per-tenant pin controls, but can be adapted to hosted routes via client-routing headers.

High-level idea (phase-interleave)
1) Define phases (P0, P1, P2) that represent 10–20% client slices depending on fleet size.
2) For a model flip from M-A -> M-B: assign each client to an anchor phase + sub-phase (A/B).
3) At any time, at least one sub-phase remains pinned to previous model to absorb error/latency regressions.
4) Rotate pin state on a tight cadence (e.g., every 30m for warmup sensitive routes, 2h for high-cost routes) so heat spreads without bulk cold starts.

Concrete schedule example (50 clients, 3 phases)
- Phase sizes: P0=20, P1=15, P2=15 (approx).
- Sub-phase state per phase: (Pinned -> Candidate -> Observing) sequences staggered so P0 pinned while P1 candidate, P2 observing; next window, rotate states.
- Windows: 30m windows for chat endpoints that rely on KV cache, 1h for text-only generation, 2h for very large models.

Checklist (preflight)
- [ ] Confirm client cohort mapping (export list + identify high-traffic tenants).
- [ ] Ensure model artifacts present across all regions and quant variants are compatible.
- [ ] Bake short warmup prompt set (10 prompts) per route. Keep prompts deterministic and fast.
- [ ] Confirm telemetry dashboards have these metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate, token throughput, CPU/GPU utilization, cache hit ratio, model fallback rate.
- [ ] Create Alert/Slack hooks for exceed thresholds.
- [ ] Dry-run: simulate rotation in staging using recorded traffic replay.

Observability signals to watch (primary -> secondary)
- Primary: p99 latency spike (+25% baseline), error rate > 0.5% absolute, model fallback count > 5 per minute.
- Secondary: sustained increase in token generation time, KV cache miss rate > 10% (relative), GPU mem pressure > 70% for 10+ minutes.
- Canary-specific: per-cohort quality regressions detected by eval probes (synthetic prompt suite).

Rollback / escape plan
- Immediate: pin traffic back to last-known-good model for the affected phase. Keep other phases rotating unchanged to avoid a full cold restart.
- If multiple phases show regressions: trigger regional failover to lower-capacity but stable variant (quantized or smaller model) and start gradual backfill.
- Postmortem action: identify trigger (prompt distribution shift, kernel selection change, quantization mismatch). Add probe prompts to the warmup set.

Warmup prompts & budget
- Keep 8–12 warmup prompts per route: short, deterministic, cached prefixes where applicable.
- Budget per window: <= 1000 tokens per 1k users for small models; scale up for high memory models but cap cost.
- Use streaming events to measure first-byte latency and KV priming effectiveness.

Traffic shaping rules (implementation snippets)
- Routing policy must support annotated cohort headers (X-Client-Cohort). Use sticky pins per client id for duration of rotation.
- If using SDK toggles: set per-tenant pin TTL slightly longer than rotation to avoid flapping (rotation + 10%).

Edge cases / gotchas
- Tenant churn: new tenant onboarding during rotation may become pinned to a cold variant; consider assigning new tenants to Observing sub-phase first.
- Quota & throttling: warmups can trigger QPS spikes; gate warmups behind token budget and ramp by linear backoff.
- Mixed-model fallbacks: ensure compatibility maps for KVs and embeddings when fallback triggers.

Experiment instrumentation (hypothesis-driven)
- H0: Phase-interleave reduces p99 tail frequency by 30% during flip windows compared to single-burst flip.
- Metric mix: freq(p99> threshold), mean cache hit, warmup cost per user, % of phases rolled back.
- Experiment run: A/B split by customer segments (non-critical vs critical tenants) for 3 full rotations.

Small script ideas / commands (staging)
- export cohort -> cohorts.csv
- simulate-rotation --cohort-file cohorts.csv --model-a M-A --model-b M-B --window 30m --stagger 10m
- check-probes --suite warmup-10 --region us-west1

Communication playbook (who says what)
- On deviation: on-call SRE posts in #deploy-ops with short header: "phase-interleave deviation: P1 p99 spike 35% (us-west1)" and links to dashboard + cohort list.
- Escalation: after 15m without improvement, paging to release lead and eng on-call.

Open questions / TODOs for follow-up
- Decide canonical phase sizing algorithm (fixed percentage vs traffic-weighted).
- Add adaptive rotation (longer for heavy models, shorter for small routes) into rollout engine.
- Tighten alert thresholds: run short calibration in staging.
- Write a lightweight SDK helper to compute cohort header per tenant at signup.

Quick decision log (notes to self)
- Prefer smaller early windows (30m) for chat because KV priming matters; use 2h for >2B parameter models.
- Keep at least one phase pinned at all times for safety.
- For Private deployments, surface phase metadata in admin UI so customers can opt-out of interleaving.

If this works in staging: draft a short runbook and a one-pager for Product/Success outlining expected customer-visible behavior and how to opt-out.

End of notebook.

-----
Scratchpad additions while iterating:
- Maybe use a rolling hash on client-id to compute phase assignment so it's stable and deterministic.
- Consider warmup priming via low-cost embedding calls to preheat tokenizers/weights before full-gen warmups.
- Add a small randomized jitter to rotation time (±1–3m) to prevent synchronized effects across regions.
